questions.question: Give three uses of metals in the home and the property that makes each metal suitable.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: pots and kettles, because metals conduct heat and have high melting points; steel chair frames, because steel is strong; gold or silver jewellery, because it is shiny and does not rust; coins, because metal is hard and lasts.

questions.question: Why is copper used for electrical wires and steel for fences and roofs?
questions.expected_answer: Copper is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wire, and it conducts electricity very well. Steel is strong and ductile for fence wire, and malleable and strong for roofing sheets, which are galvanised or painted so they do not rust.

questions.question: Why are steel and aluminium used in cars, buildings and bridges, and why should metals be recycled?
questions.expected_answer: Steel is very strong and malleable, so it carries heavy loads in bridges and building frames and can be pressed into car body shapes. Aluminium is light and does not rust, so it is used for car wheels and window frames. Metals should be recycled because they can be melted and reused again and again, which saves energy and ore and reduces waste.
